title: The week nobody circled (वो हफ़्ता जिस पर गोला नहीं था)
look: Station railway posters: flat poster colour, bold simple shapes, a railway poster's sky, painted over a present-day station road and the family's electrical shop facing the platform. Phones, steel glasses, plastic stools, fans and switches in plain cardboard boxes with no labels. No letters, numbers, logos or signatures anywhere; every board, box and paper is painted blank.
goals: Target 1, Clean-up and counter: 2 days late or fewer (each pick in decisions 1 and 5, the plain team twin, set A). The equal two are late 1 and 2, so either clears it.
Target 2, Roof and sorting: 3 days free or more (the top 2 in decisions 3 and 7, the plain rank twin, set B). The equal two have 4 and 5 days free.
Fixed line for the matters twin (decisions 2 and 6), the same for every pick: Tempo: back. New stock: in.
Stamp on Station's split-flap tiles: Shutter up 9:00 (both targets met) / 9:30 (one) / 10:15 (none). Hard twin (decisions 4 and 8) feeds nothing.

The station road in July rain, seen from across the road: the family's electrical shop with its rolling shutter half raised and brown water over the step, the platform beyond with an empty bench and a blank cream name board. The event, painted once for every band. Saturday morning on the station road, seen from across the road: the shutter fully up, the shop lit, fans in plain boxes on the shelves, a few passengers from the platform crossing at a distance with their backs turned. Mummy seen from behind at the counter, left third. On the platform, Station's split-flap board painted blank, where the stamp lands as live tiles (the world's big moment), reading 9:00, 9:30 or 10:15 by band. Nobody from the cards. Only Mummy's line changes with the band; the picture, the sound of the tiles and your reply never do. MARKS: [WAITS rulebook Q5 and options Q15: the stamp says how the event went, between chapters] [BREAKS rule 42: the close runs four beats (event with the reaction, the stamped list, the fixed ending, progress), not two or three, because the stamped list (rule 43) and the bible's fixed ending each need a picture] Counted per band: at most 12 EN / 15 HI.

beats.painting: Present day, between chapters. The kitchen calendar: the July week now circled in pencil with a small shutter drawn inside it, beside the red circle on 15 August. The three red circles and the two pencil ones differ in line and shape as well as colour. No score, no lean, no row of picks.

writer_notes: RULES 15 AND 17 PULL AGAINST EACH OTHER HERE, so one has to give, and you choose which. With ten people, two fixed number sets and the bible's eight pairs, a search script scored tens of millions of line-ups and number sets. The best designs it found with four decisions holding a second same-sex tie (rule 15) all had at least two pairs who arrive with different earlier showings (rule 17), and each either gave several people the same years (everyone on 4) or left a numbers-only player never facing the two in decision 5 (rule 14). This chapter keeps the numbers clean and every decision fair to a numbers-only player (rule 14), and marks the cost: two same-sex ties (decisions 4 and 8) instead of four, and two pairs who do not match on earlier showings (decisions 3 and 6). Ways out, for you: twelve people a chapter, a third number set, or rule 17 counting only how many cards each of the two was on.

Breaks marked on beats: rule 15 (six decisions with no second tie), rule 17 (decisions 3 and 6), rule 21 (Francis is the weakest card in decisions 6, 7 and 8, and no Christian name ever tops a decision), rule 42 (four closing beats). Waits marked: rulebook Q5, Q6, Q11, Q14, Q16 and options Q11, Q15; rule 23 (are the 6 am keys and the cash drawer a gain?) and rule 28 (the bullying pair for the five Hindi-first readers).

Kusum is the weakest card in decisions 1, 2, 4 and 5, and she and Francis are the only cards that miss a bar (Kusum in 1 and 5, Francis in 3 and 7). The misses are 2 women and 2 men, as rule 45 asks, but the two who always miss are the oldest woman and an older Christian man, which a reader may take as "the old ones lose". Only a bigger circle fixes it.

Changes from the bible, none silent: Asha is 33 not 36 (a new face, so nothing to repaint), so "who is older" changes side between the halves of twins A and B (rule 17). Decision 2 asks "Who gets the tempo to the godown?" rather than "drives", because "driving" is in two of its card notes (rule 36). Decision 6's licence note is new words ("Licensed to ride a two-wheeler"), not a one-word swap of decision 2's "Holds a driving licence" (rules 6 and 16). The rank questions say "places", because "work" and "job" sat in card notes.

The pairs, sets, kinds and nudge sides are the bible's. Card line-ups and every number are new, checked by scratchpad/blend/build_ch3.py and ch3_search.py: one woman-and-man tie per decision; numbers-only players always face the equal two (pick one: they lead on both numbers; team: two cards above them on each number; rank: one above); nobody who was weakest earlier sits in a later pair; each paired bar sits at or below the equal two.

Outcome check over all 40,000 answer sets for the four decisions that feed targets: swapping the equal two never changes the band, "always the woman" and "always the man" both end at 9:00, and all three bands can happen. The matters and hard twins change nothing. No line names a person; the counts on the list follow only the numbers.

Words, counted with speech (rulebook Q14 still open): the story beats come to 97 English and 110 Hindi counted words (cap 120 each); no beat over 20 or more than 3 pieces; every spoken line 10 words or fewer and every narration 12 or fewer; questions 8 words or fewer. The title card counts 18/20 as a cover. Closing beats stay under 20 per band.

Notes: every card has one, in the applicants' slips; within 2 words of each other in both languages; the equal two the same length with different opening words and frames; the longest note sits on the two in 2 of 8 decisions (7 alone, 8 shared). Each plain decision has a second judging remark from the same voice; Mummy's remarks fall on 2 women and 2 men, Masterji's on 2 women and 2 men (rule 22). Heavy-sounding decoy facts on unmarked names in both hard decisions (Kusum in 4, Rohit in 8). Against type: dhaba cook, uniform stitcher, tuition teacher, cake baker and tiffin cook among the men; kabaddi, truck loading, tiling, house painting and a bottling plant among the women.

Hindi: every line by or to you uses forms that mark no gender (polite commands to Mummy, the subjunctive in every "who should" question, no verbs in your two lines). The scan in build_ch3.py still catches 10 lines (करे, रहे, मिले, जाए, and nouns such as बजे or मज़दूरी before a full stop); none fixes a gender, and each waits for a native reader to clear, as rule 66 asks. Buttons use the game's आप (चुनें, भेजें); Mummy's questions use तुम commands (चुनो, क्रम लगाओ).

Twins match in shape: the same asker (Mummy), one question bubble each, words within 2, and lead-ins with the same figures (Mummy from behind before 1 and 5, and before 3 and 7; a people-free shop picture with a clock and one sound before 2 and 6, and before 4 and 8). The hard questions sit in the plain question box. The hard twin's first half is at decision 4 (chapters 1 and 4 use 3, chapters 2 and 5 use 2), so rule 25 holds.

As the task asked, every decision is followed by one short "it happened" beat, the same for every pick (mostly one sound word); the bible had them only at a change of place. There is no reply bubble from you after a pick, so options Q14 does not arise here; the settled plates show job words only.

Six-player test (rule 1): the family shop is this take's weakest chapter for the metro puzzle player and the retired officer; readers decide. The flood itself is written as "the station road is under water", with no real place, law or figure.

For painting later (not now): five new faces in the Station look (Asha, Sapna, Kavita, Vinod, Pankaj) with the close-up check for painted dots and lightened skin; Masterji's chapter portrait; glossary rows and one reference picture each for the key ring with its plain brass tag, the half-raised rolling shutter, the hired tempo under a plain tarpaulin, the blank split-flap board, fans in plain boxes, the ruled paper list, the steel cash drawer, the scooter with a plain helmet and the open padlock.
